source.title: Latent-space adversarial training with post-aware calibration for defending large language models against jailbreak attacks
source.authors: Xin Yi; Yue Li; Dong-Sheng Shi; Linlin Wang; Xiaoling Wang; Liang He

record.tranche_reason: The study applies a mask-based perturbation derived from harmful–harmless activation differences at different decoder block locations and reports harmful-output attack success rates. This is a conceptual test of whether removal of refusal-related features can elicit harmful compliance, but it does not test the original single-direction, all-layer ablation.
record.gate_note: The reported block-position results in Table 5 directly evaluate the study's refusal-feature perturbation and are recorded below. The broader LATPC benchmark results evaluate the authors' combined training and calibration method, not the refusal direction itself, so they are not rows. Figure 8 reports activation similarities by layer and token position, but does not report a refusal-behavior outcome.
record.test_reason: This is a jailbreak-defense paper (LATPC). It uses a masked, scaled harmful-minus-harmless feature subtraction only as the simulated attack inside adversarial training, and its headline results measure the defense. Table 5 is a design ablation choosing where to inject that attack. It does not say which model or checkpoint was used, gives no unperturbed baseline, and applies a modified intervention (top-30% lowest-variance dimensions, λ=0.6, at selected layers). Its ASRs therefore cannot show whether a single difference-in-means direction mediates refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that LATPC (variance-selected refusal-feature removal attack plus latent adversarial training, and inference-time post-aware calibration) lowers jailbreak ASR across five attacks and four models while limiting over-refusal and preserving MMLU/TriviaQA. They take the refusal-feature account from Arditi et al. as given rather than testing it.
record.recipe_differences: The study selects stable, low-variance dimensions of harmful–harmless activation differences and applies a masked feature perturbation at selected decoder locations. It uses this perturbation for adversarial training and adds inference-time calibration; it does not project out one direction at every layer and position or add that direction to induce refusals.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported attack success rate varies across the four injection locations and three datasets; the authors state Post-Layer has the highest ASR. The text also says Top-k and perturbation strength lambda affect ASR and perplexity, and that the final token position is most discriminative for the reported activation similarity analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: A masked, scaled subtraction of the harmful–harmless mean difference (top-30% low-variance dimensions, λ=0.6) raises harmful ASR to at most 38.6/21.6/31.8 on HarmBench/AdvBench/JailbreakBench. Post-Layer injection is strongest; Attention/MLP outputs give only 3–9%. Model unstated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partial, dimension-masked removal of refusal features elicits only modest harmful compliance, and the effect depends strongly on injection site.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA at layer 28 (Fig. 7, A.1, A.2) shows jailbreak-prompt representations converging toward harmless queries, with no direction projection or behavioral link.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak prompts move harmful-query representations toward the harmless cluster (geometry only).

record.problems: Table 5 provides no unperturbed baseline or uncertainty estimates, and does not state the model/checkpoint for those results. The feature perturbation is not the original single-direction intervention; no all-layer ablation, addition intervention, or direct general-capability test of that ablation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded the LATPC benchmark outcomes in Tables 1–4 and Appendix Table A.3 because they measure the combined defense method rather than the refusal-feature removal itself. Excluded the Figure 8 activation-similarity results because they show representation geometry rather than refusal behavior.

untested.parts: No full difference-in-means direction ablation across all layers and positions, no addition test, and no capability check of the ablation.

Does not measure whether real jailbreaks suppress the direction (only PCA geometry). Robustness is reported for the combined LATPC method and for a reimplemented ReFAT baseline, not as an isolated test.

record.verdict_notes: Classified T4 because refusal-feature removal serves only as a training-time attack. A possible V3-relevant signal sits in the method-comparison tables, not in any row. The reimplemented ReFAT baseline (training against refusal-feature ablation) cuts ASR on many attacks but barely on Adaptive Attack (Llama3-8B 91.8→88.1; Mistral 94.3→96.9; Table 1/3). LATPC without PAC gives Adaptive ASR 67.9 vs vanilla 91.8 (Table 4). These are defense-method comparisons with a modified intervention, so they are left as context, not verdicts. The Table 5 subject is likely Llama3-8B but not stated.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test a single unmasked difference-in-means direction, ablation at every layer and position, adding the direction, or general abilities after the original ablation. The reported fluency proxy does not establish preservation of general capability.
No practical weight-edit removal or released-model abliteration is tested.
The study does not establish that real jailbreak attacks suppress this direction, or isolate robustness gained specifically from training against ablation of the original direction.
The study does not compare a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account of refusal.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
The study does not test whether refusal training determines the existence of a removable direction.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Mask-based refusal-feature perturbations at the four reported decoder block locations across HarmBench, AdvBench, and JailbreakBench
reader_labels.reason: The intervention yields partial ASR rather than showing refusal removal, and the reported outcomes vary by injection location and dataset; it is not the claimed all-layer single-direction ablation (rows T5-HB-PRE-ASR through T5-JB-POST-ASR).
